Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  - Acute watery diarrhoea for ~3 days, frequency ~5–6 bowel motions/day.
  - Initial vomiting for a couple of episodes; vomiting has stopped.
  - Reports feeling dehydrated, decreased oral intake and poor appetite, generalized weakness.
  - Possible transient low-grade fever noted at onset; currently feels "kind of fine."
  - No visible blood in stools.
  - Working as a software engineer; recently off work for past 3 days due to illness.
  - Clinician assessed as probable gastroenteritis (tummy bug).

- Relevant family medical history:
  - Father: history of hypertension; died of bowel (colorectal) cancer ~10 years ago.

Management Plan

- Summary of key management actions and recommendations:
  - Clinician diagnosis: probable gastroenteritis.
  - Advise increased oral fluid intake; recommendation to use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) to replenish electrolytes.
  - Paracetamol advised for fever/weakness if required.
  - Advise rest and continue time off work for 1–2 additional days; recommended to be diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours before returning to work.
  - Return visit advised if symptoms persist beyond one week.

- Immediate interventions:
  - Symptomatic management only (oral fluids, ORS, paracetamol). No medications prescribed during consult.

- Follow-up appointments or patient education:
  - Return to clinic if not improved within a week.
  - Patient instructed to call back if symptoms worsen or do not resolve.

- Referrals:
  - No allied health, sexual health, or mental health referrals were made.
  - No preventative health follow-up booked.
